Endorsed by the Walnut Creek Teachers Association
# Listen first. Lead better.
Aileen Ong has spent 20+ years helping organizations like Google and PayPal communicate clearly and reach the right audiences. Last spring, she saw Walnut Creek School District (WCSD)'s own communication problem up close, and decided sitting on the sidelines wasn't an option. Now she's running for WCSD Governing Board. The district needs a board that listens before deciding, and explains clearly after.
Meet Aileen Donate
The Problem
## WCSD Has a Communication Problem
Parents find out about big decisions after they're made. Questions get asked and go unanswered. Budgets get approved with no plain-language explanation of where the money goes.
Last spring, Tice Creek School lost its principal. 200+ parents signed a petition asking the district to listen. Families showed up and asked questions. The district appointed a new principal anyway, without input from parents or staff.
Then came Measure L. 64% of voters said yes, but the parcel tax needed two-thirds. That gap wasn't about whether people value good schools. It was trust: voters want to know exactly where their money goes, and too many didn't get a clear enough answer.
Different issues. Same problem: WCSD isn't communicating well enough with the people it serves.
Aileen knows how to fix that.
Meet Aileen
A communications strategist. A current WCSD parent. Ready to bring both to the board.
Communications is Aileen's profession, not just a talking point. She's spent 20+ years helping organizations build trust and get people to act, the same skill set she brought to Tice Creek this spring.
She's also spent years showing up for Walnut Creek schools as a PTA secretary, room parent, classroom volunteer, crossing guard, and Girl Scout leader.
When Tice Creek families needed someone to organize, she stepped up. Aileen spoke at board meetings, worked with reporters, and kept pushing for answers.
She holds a B.A. from UC Berkeley and an MBA from UCLA.
Aileen lives in Walnut Creek with her husband and two daughters, both WCSD students.
She knows how to listen, explain complicated issues clearly, and bring people together. That's what she'll bring to the board.

Why I'm running
## Walnut Creek schools are strong. Our board can be stronger.
"I didn't set out to run for school board. I set out to get a straight answer. When I couldn't get one, I realized this district needed someone who knows how to fix that."
Aileen believes board members should show up before decisions are made—not after.
That means visiting schools. Asking hard questions. Hearing from families and staff. And explaining the reasoning behind important decisions.
Listen first. Lead better.
That's how Aileen would govern.
Measure L
### 64% said yes. It still failed.
Aileen believes the lesson isn't to simply ask voters again.
It's for the board to earn their trust first. That's part of why she's running.
Taxpayers deserve clear answers:
- What are we paying for?
- Why is it needed?
- What will students get?
- How will we know it worked?
And that conversation can't start when the district needs a vote. It has to happen all year long—with parents, staff, and taxpayers across Walnut Creek.
Related: our local high schools (Acalanes, Campolindo, Las Lomas, and Miramonte) are facing a similar funding fight this fall — learn about Measure W →
The Platform
## Listen. Lead. Invest.
Three ways to fix one root problem: a district that doesn't communicate well enough with the people it serves.
### Listen
Hear people before you decide.
- Visit every school before major decisions affecting it.
- Talk directly with families and staff.
- Bring community input in early.
### Lead
Make decisions in the open.
- Clear processes for major appointments and policy decisions.
- Ask hard questions. Expect clear answers.
- Do the work before casting the vote.
### Invest
Respect every taxpayer.
- Make budgets easier to understand.
- Clearly explain what we're spending and why.
- Show the connection between dollars spent and student outcomes.

“As a WCSD parent and the owner of The Ballet School, which is celebrating 50 years in our community, I know how important it is to have people who are truly invested in our schools and our community.
My grandfather, George Denison, served as a trustee on the Walnut Creek School Board, so community involvement has always been especially meaningful to our family. I'm so proud of Aileen for stepping up to run. I love that she's taking a truly grassroots approach and making the effort to meet and listen to as many people as she can. I'm honored to support her. She can absolutely count on my vote!”
JP
Jenny Perry
WCSD Parent & Owner, The Ballet School
“I've known Aileen Ong for nearly 30 years, since we were freshmen together at UC Berkeley... Her candidacy gives me confidence that we can continue building on WCSD's strengths while bringing new perspective to its governance.”
Read David's full letter →Show less
“Long before either of us imagined raising families in Walnut Creek, we knew each other as classmates and friends. It means something to me that, decades later, we have both chosen to make this community our home and to invest ourselves in the strength of its public schools.
Walnut Creek has much to be proud of. Strong public schools are one of the reasons families choose to build their lives here. But strong institutions do not stay strong by reputation alone. They require thoughtful leadership, clear communication, good judgment, and a willingness to remain connected and accountable to the full community they serve.
Her message of “Listen first. Lead better.” is not, to me, an argument that boards should simply do whatever the loudest group of parents asks. Great governance requires something harder: listening broadly, asking serious questions, understanding perspectives that may not naturally make their way into the room, and then making decisions transparently and explaining the reasoning behind them.
This matters especially in public education. Not every family has the same amount of time, institutional knowledge, financial capacity, or comfort navigating school systems. Trustees represent all of them. The families deeply involved in PTA and WCEF matter, and so do multilingual families, families receiving public assistance, families new to the district, and parents who may never attend a board meeting. Strong governance requires intentionally understanding all of these experiences.
I also believe board service should add value. Trustees should respect the professional responsibilities of the superintendent and educators while bringing independent judgment, curiosity, oversight, and a deep understanding of the community to the decisions entrusted to them. Their work should make the institution more thoughtful, more transparent, and ultimately stronger.
I know Aileen personally, and I know the seriousness she brings to questions of communication, trust, and responsibility. As a fellow Walnut Creek parent, I appreciate her willingness to step forward and serve a community that has given our families so much.”
DL
David Lazo
WCSD Parent & Buena Vista Site Council
“As a WCSD parent, I'm very happy to endorse Aileen Ong for the Walnut Creek School District Governing Board. What really stands out to me is that Aileen isn't looking at our schools from the outside.”

“She is a parent with children currently in the district who has been actively involved in our school community, so she understands firsthand the issues families are experiencing and the importance of making sure parents, educators, and students are heard. After hearing her speak and learning more about what she hopes to bring to the Board, I believe she would bring a valuable perspective, greater transparency, and thoughtful, engaged leadership to our district.”
JS
Judy Sosa
Parent, Walnut Creek Intermediate

FAQ
## Common questions
### Why do you keep talking about communication?
Because it's fundamental to good governance.
People should understand what the district is doing, why it's doing it, and how their voices fit into the process.
Better communication builds trust. Trust makes better decisions possible.
### Is this a partisan race?
No. WCSD Governing Board is a nonpartisan office. Aileen will listen to everyone in the community, regardless of party.
### How can I help the campaign?
Volunteer your time, chip in what you can, or just show up. Every bit helps.
### What do you think about technology and AI in classrooms?
I hear about AI from parents everywhere I go, and it's a fair question. Our kids already have access to more technology than any generation before them.
Here's where I stand: our students do not need new tech tools, including AI, added to their education right now. Our teachers already have plenty of tools at their disposal, and I'm not looking to add more - unless teachers themselves tell me it's a need.
On the board, I'll take my cues from the people in the classroom. I'll rely on teachers' professional judgment about what actually helps them teach, and I'll listen to parents' concerns about what's right for their kids. And I'll be watching closely what unfolds in places like Los Angeles and New York before we bring anything new into our own classrooms.
Decisions about classroom technology should start with educators and families, not vendors.
In the Press
Aileen put her communications experience to work this spring. She brought the Tice Creek story to a reporter, then wrote and placed two letters to the editor herself, rallying fellow parents to sign on.
